claims.head: The Senators will send their checkers at Stenberg
claims.call: The Senators’ L4 (Cousins, Pinto and Amadio) spends at least 34% of its 5-on-5 time against the Sharks’ second line.
claims.body: At home, the Senators keep sending Pinto’s line (Cousins, Pinto and Amadio) out against opponents’ second lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Travis Green has been using this group as a checking line on opponents’ second lines. Tonight the Sharks’ second line is Stenberg, Misa and Sherwood.

claims.gist: At home, Travis Green likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Sharks’ second line.

notes.text: Alexander Wennberg is out week to week (upper body injury) and missed their last game. He is a top-six forward. Collin Graf has taken his spot beside Tyler Toffoli and Mason Marchment.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 28% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the fifth-lowest in the league (a typical team: 41%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Thomas Chabot is out 1-2 weeks (upper body injury) and missed their last game. He is a top-pair defenseman. Tyler Kleven has taken his spot beside Jordan Spence.
William Eklund is out 10-12 weeks and has missed the last 6 games.
Jake Sanderson returned in their last game after missing 8 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Artem Zub was added to the roster on Oct 16 and has played beside Thomas Chabot.
Jordan Spence has started killing penalties: on the ice for 35% of the team’s shorthanded time in 10 games, up from 4% last season.

OTT.head: Advantage, the Senators
OTT.body: Even though Ottawa is on the second night of a back-to-back, the Senators have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. The Sharks can make it interesting if they keep shots to a minimum.

SJS.head: A tough matchup for the Sharks
SJS.body: Even though Ottawa is on the second night of a back-to-back, the Senators have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. The Sharks can pull it off if they keep shots to a minimum.

story.head: Who’s in net for the Senators?
paras: The Sharks come in at 5-4-1, the Senators at 7-3-0.
